course_goals.text: Analyze the fundamental concepts, history, and scope of Extended Reality (XR) systems by defining the reality-virtuality continuum and classifying various XR technologies.
Evaluate the impact of human factors and sensory perception on immersive experience, including analyzing biological limitations, the causes of cybersickness, and the role of multi-sensory design.
Design and implement user-centered interactive systems by applying principles of usability, interaction design, and complex locomotion techniques.
Engineer XR applications by mastering the architecture of modern hardware, advanced tracking methodologies, and the computer graphics rendering pipeline.
Validate, optimize, and deploy XR systems by conducting rigorous empirical evaluations, applying system optimization algorithms, and utilizing professional development tools.

L01.lecture_goal: introduce the foundational concepts and current scope of Extended Reality (XR) systems.

objectives.text: identify the common terms (XR, VR, AR, and MR) and differentiate between initial perceptions of various immersive technologies
define extended reality (XR) and differentiate between Augmented Reality, Augmented Virtuality, and Mixed Reality along the reality-virtuality continuum
explain the growing commercial and technological interest in virtual and augmented reality fields and outline the key objectives and curriculum roadmap for the XR systems course
relate the concepts of XR, AR, MR, and VR within the overarching reality-virtuality continuum

L02.lecture_goal: Categorize and distinguish various extended reality and virtual reality systems based on their application domains and technological architecture.

objectives.text: you'll be able to identify and describe the various application domains and system categories for extended reality and virtual reality technologies
you'll be able to differentiate between non-immersive, semi-immersive, and fully immersive VR system categories based on their characteristics and varying degrees of user immersion

L03.lecture_goal: compare and contrast the application domains, technical categories, and system characteristics of augmented and virtual reality.

objectives.text: identify and distinguish various application domains for augmented reality, including examples across different industries of virtual and augmented reality systems
categorize augmented reality applications by their underlying technology, detailing the characteristics and subcategories of both marker-based and markerless systems
compare the fundamental system categories of VR and AR based on their respective experiences and underlying technology

L04.lecture_goal: Analyze and apply the fundamental definitional characteristics to evaluate various real-world systems as Virtual Reality.

objectives.text: distinguish between virtual and real based on definitional characteristics, define Virtual Reality, and identify its three essential components: artificial environment, sensory experience, and interaction
evaluate whether a given system or real-world application meets the requirements of a Virtual Reality system by verifying its three essential characteristics

L05.lecture_goal: differentiate the core concepts and characteristics of augmented, virtual, and mixed reality systems.

objectives.text: define augmented reality and identify its essential and systemic defining characteristics
compare and distinguish between augmented reality, virtual reality, and mixed reality systems

L06.lecture_goal: trace the complete historical development and key innovations of virtual reality technology.

objectives.text: identify the four historical phases of virtual reality evolution
trace the conceptual and technological evolution of virtual reality from early inventions through the late 1980s
you'll be able to describe the major hardware and software developments and identify key milestones during the modern (1990-2015) and growth (2016 onwards) phases of virtual reality

L07.lecture_goal: Trace the historical progression of augmented and virtual reality systems from their conceptual beginnings to their current commercial applications.

objectives.text: identify the distinct historical phases of augmented reality and trace the foundational research, key figures, and early developments that shaped virtual and augmented reality systems
outline the key technological and application advancements achieved during the tools and applications phase (mid-1990s to early 2000s)
you'll be able to summarize the commercial growth phases and future trends of Augmented Reality

L08.lecture_goal: Analyze the fundamental issues and challenges that define the quality and scope of virtual reality experiences.

objectives.text: review the fundamental concepts, characteristics, and major challenges associated with VR and AR systems
define immersion, identify the objective degrees that characterize a VR experience, and explain the six qualitative terms contributing to it

you'll be able to compare and distinguish between technological immersion and psychological presence, and understand how immersion supports the achievement of presence within virtual reality experiences

L09.lecture_goal: Analyze the foundational theories, perception challenges, and technical requirements guiding the development of immersive virtual and augmented reality systems.

objectives.text: compare the different definitions of reality (mimicry versus transcendence) that inform the design of virtual reality systems
explain the Uncanny Valley effect and define the types of fidelity necessary for developing believable virtual environments
explain the technological requirements and functional phases (registration and tracking) needed for an augmented reality system to function
you'll be able to identify the core concepts and challenges (such as immersion, presence, and the Uncanny Valley) related to the use of VR and AR systems

L10.lecture_goal: Analyze the various internal and external factors that contribute to cybersickness.

objectives.text: you'll be able to identify the symptoms of cybersickness and outline the three key aspects of addressing it
you'll be able to explain how diverse internal factors and specific hardware elements contribute to cybersickness

L11.lecture_goal: comprehend the causes of cybersickness and analyze the various methods available for its measurement.

objectives.text: explain how specific content factors (like visual motion, locomotion, FOV, and complexity) influence the onset and severity of cybersickness
identify and differentiate between the four main input types (questionnaire, physiological, behavioral, and content-based) and contrast manual and automated methods used to measure cybersickness

L12.lecture_goal: Explore the causes, evaluation methods, and various mitigation strategies for cybersickness in immersive experiences.

objectives.text: understand how cybersickness is studied and modeled, by being able to categorize the components of cybersickness evaluation, recognize various measurement techniques, differentiate between black box and interpretable models, and distinguish evaluation techniques based on the measurement event and output type

analyze the technical strategies for mitigation, by being able to analyze the challenges and trade-offs involved in mitigating cybersickness while maintaining user presence, explain how FOV adjustment techniques work, identify and describe various techniques like blur and optical flow manipulation, and describe hardware alterations and locomotion techniques used to reduce cybersickness

synthesize the knowledge base, by being able to describe the user's role and practical countermeasures needed, identify user-based strategies to mitigate effects, and review the causes, measurement, and mitigation approaches for cybersickness

L13.lecture_goal: analyze the complete architecture of VR systems by examining their foundational components and diverse methods of user input.

objectives.text: understand how a comprehensive VR system functions by defining its elements, data flows, and the roles of the user, hardware, and environment
identify the three major categories of VR hardware, including displays, sensors, and computers
compare various hand-based input devices—such as tracked and non-tracked controllers, pinch gloves, and bare hand techniques—and analyze their impact on user presence and system limitations
differentiate between non-hand-based input devices, like head and eye trackers, and explain the challenges inherent in technologies such as eye-tracking to necessitate multimodal input

L14.lecture_goal: Analyze the fundamental components and systems that constitute modern VR hardware.

objectives.text: compare and describe non-hand input methods, such as full-body tracking and voice tracking, used in VR systems
compare the various processing elements and identify the roles and requirements of GPU, CPU, and RAM in VR systems
differentiate between types of visual displays and output devices, including HMDs, world-fixed displays, specialized audio, haptics, and motion platforms

L15.lecture_goal: analyze the diverse landscape of augmented reality by understanding its key hardware categories, components, and enabling technologies.

objectives.text: you'll be able to categorize and compare the various types and components of augmented reality devices, including smart glasses, headsets, and handheld devices
you'll be able to differentiate spatial augmented reality devices and describe the underlying spatial layer systems and display technologies that enable them
you'll be able to summarize and categorize the five major types of AR hardware systems discussed in the lecture

L16.lecture_goal: Master the concepts and processes of tracking systems used in immersive reality applications.

objectives.text: understand the fundamental requirements of tracking by differentiating its purpose in Virtual Reality (VR) versus Augmented Reality (AR) and categorizing the elements being tracked (user, body parts, or environment)

analyze tracking methodologies by comparing outside-in and inside-out approaches based on sensor placement and operational constraints, and detailing the four major computational steps involved (calibration, registration, integration, and drift correction)
summarize the core concepts of the tracking process by explaining the elements tracked, the core methods utilized, and the sequential stages of the entire process

L17.lecture_goal: comprehend the fundamental components, operational stages, and error correction methods used in modern tracking systems.

objectives.text: identify the types of tracked objects and the four stages of operation, and describe the components and function of Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs) in tracking systems

explain the process of calibrating imperfect sensor data by mathematically modeling and correcting measurement errors, and detail the steps of registration and integration for setting initial alignment and tracking orientation

apply techniques, such as blending sensor values using a gain parameter, to correct drift errors in orientation estimation, and describe how virtual reality tracking systems function through the phases of calibration, registration, and drift correction

L18.lecture_goal: Understand the principles and applications of various tracking systems used to enable real-time positioning and interaction in VR and AR environments.

objectives.text: categorize and describe the basic hardware components and types of electromechanical trackers used in VR and AR systems (L18/P01-L18/P02)
explain the operating principles and describe the features of various sensor-based tracking methods, including electromagnetic, acoustic, infrared, and visible light tracking (L18/P03-L18/P07)
understand how advanced model-based techniques like SLAM and 3D structure tracking enable real-time, drift-free pose registration in augmented reality (L18/P08-L18/P09)
differentiate between various system-level trackers, such as inertial and GPS, by analyzing their functions, limitations, and overall applications in VR and AR (L18/P10-L18/P11)

L19.lecture_goal: understand the foundational principles, design processes, and interactive mechanisms governing VR software development.

objectives.text: explain the role of VR software in translating user actions into sensory experiences, detailing the complete data flow loop and necessary design considerations between the user and the VR hardware
compare development methodologies and identify the core processes and components required to create synthetic and real virtual worlds
analyze how VR software manages user movement, addressing the challenges of matched motion and the mismatch between physical and virtual locomotion

L20.lecture_goal: understand the complete lifecycle of VR software, from fundamental components and system architecture to tool selection and final deployment.

objectives.text: you'll be able to describe the abstract components, physics requirements, and networking demands essential for constructing immersive, realistic, and collaborative virtual worlds

you'll be able to analyze development strategies by comparing the benefits of building from scratch versus using generators, and delineate the layered architecture and core functionalities of XR game engines
you'll be able to compare native and web deployment methods, categorize available development tools, and summarize the critical choices in VR software development

L21.lecture_goal: evaluate the necessary tools and technical considerations for developing augmented reality experiences.

objectives.text: categorize various AR software tools and technologies based on required skill level, application platform, or implementation technology
compare the functions and limitations of low-level AR libraries versus combined AR frameworks
identify rapid prototyping and development tools suitable for building augmented reality experiences

L22.lecture_goal: analyze the various development methods, tool integrations, and categories that define AR software.

objectives.text: you'll be able to contrast methods for developing AR prototypes, including using frameworks and custom code
you'll be able to compare the advantages and disadvantages of using plugins and distinguish between standalone authoring tools and plugins
you'll be able to summarize the basic ideas, tools, and categories of AR software

L23.lecture_goal: Design interactive systems that are effective, efficient, and inherently focused on the needs of the human user.

objectives.text: you'll be able to explain the vision of making technology disappear from a user's perception and the importance of shielding laypersons from underlying technical complexities in interactive systems

apply the principles of user-centric design by describing the steps of the process, defining Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), and differentiating how system design must adapt to specific user characteristics and needs

L24.lecture_goal: Establish the fundamental theoretical framework and practical design principles necessary for building effective and user-centered interactive and Extended Reality systems.

objectives.text: you'll be able to understand the three-class categorization (novice, intermittent, expert) as a starting point for designing interactive systems, explain how user interface design caters to different user proficiency levels, distinguish between various professional perspectives of user-centric design and the software developer's development lifecycle, define usability by identifying its formal ISO definition, three crucial design aspects, and corresponding metrics, and define user-centered and human-centered design and categorize different types of system users

you'll be able to explain the core components and interactive data flow required for effective Extended Reality systems, and review the core concepts of interactive systems, including their design concerns and relation to XR

L25.lecture_goal: Understand the relationship between human biological limitations and perceptual science to improve the design of effective extended reality (XR) systems.

objectives.text: you'll be able to identify the role of human factors in the development of XR systems

you'll be able to explain how interaction design and perceptual design create the illusion of reality, how the human perceptual system is manipulated to achieve immersion and presence, and how biological limitations affect virtual reality experiences
you'll be able to define perceptual psychology and identify the core areas of study necessary for designing better interactive and extended reality (XR) systems
you'll be able to classify human senses and identify the specific receptors and stimuli associated with each sense organ

L26.lecture_goal: Analyze the core principles of human physiology and perception necessary for developing effective and immersive Extended Reality (XR) experiences.

objectives.text: you'll be able to describe how sensory input transitions to abstract perception using neural network concepts and explain how hierarchical processing aggregates across stages to detect complex patterns in a stimulus

you'll be able to explain how sensory signals are interpreted by integrating real-time stimuli with long-term knowledge, describe how proprioception functions as a distinct sixth sense, and explain how sensory mismatch causes cyber sickness and compromises immersion
you'll be able to summarize the fundamental principles of human physiology and perception essential for designing Virtual Reality systems

L27.lecture_goal: synthesize the fundamental principles of light physics and biological vision to understand how perception is achieved and how displays are designed.

objectives.text: explain how the human visual system and light propagation determine the design of immersive experiences in extended reality systems
describe and compare the three main ways light can be defined (photons, waves, or rays), and explain how light interacts with surfaces to determine color perception
explain how light travels through the eye, define visible light by its frequency and wavelength, and distinguish between central and peripheral vision based on photoreceptor function

L28.lecture_goal: establish the relationship between natural human visual perception and the critical design principles of modern Extended and Virtual Reality displays.

objectives.text: you'll be able to compare the optical structure and light path of the natural eye with engineered lens setups and relate human visual requirements to VR display design principles
you'll be able to explain how the field of view, binocular vision, and stereoscopy facilitate depth and three-dimensional perception

you'll be able to analyze how human visual perception of motion and 3D space dictates hardware requirements for VR and XR systems, differentiating the needs for display resolution and temporal resolution

L29.lecture_goal: relate the physical properties and biological function of sound to its role in creating immersive extended reality experiences.

objectives.text: explain the basics of the human auditory system and how auditory input supports believability, enhances perception, and increases presence in extended reality experiences
characterize sound by defining its physical properties and representing it as a wave
identify and describe the three components and specific functions of the human auditory system
explain the importance of incorporating sound alongside visual input for enhanced presence and immersion in virtual environments

L30.lecture_goal: Apply principles of human auditory perception to design and implement immersive soundscapes in extended reality (XR) systems.

objectives.text: you'll be able to distinguish the three levels of sound perception, apply psychophysical laws to predict human perception, and analyze how pitch changes with frequency

you'll be able to explain the importance of sound localization, describe the spatial parameters and binaural cues used by the auditory system, and explain how Head-Related Transfer Functions (HRTF) are utilized to implement localization effects in XR systems

L31.lecture_goal: Analyze how the integration of various human senses—including somatosensory and chemoreceptors—is essential for creating deep and full immersion experiences in XR systems.

objectives.text: you'll be able to explain how remaining senses, including touch, proprioception, and kinesthesis, create full immersive XR systems and detail the entire somatosensory perception process, from receptor activation to motor corrective action

you'll be able to identify the various types of haptic exploration and describe how these sensory interactions are implemented in XR to allow users to perceive geometric properties and build mental models of objects

you'll be able to explain how chemoreceptors process chemical stimuli for taste and smell, compare the historical and mechanical challenges of olfactory interfaces, and summarize the difficulties of simulating these chemical senses in XR

L32.lecture_goal: Master the principles and lifecycle stages required to design and develop usable interactive and extended reality systems.

objectives.text: explain the relationship between XR systems, interactive systems, and the fundamental principles of user-centric design
analyze why a systematic software development lifecycle is necessary to manage the complexity of designing usable interactive systems
describe the necessity of an iterative development process, including its stages, unique evaluation methods, and internal inter-stage loops, for building usable interactive systems
outline the broad stages of the Interactive System Development Lifecycle (ISDLC) and connect them to the development of extended reality systems

L33.lecture_goal: Introduce the Majuli case study to establish the cultural significance, preservation urgency, and technological solution for a threatened heritage site.

objectives.text: outline the scope, define the characteristics, and understand the pressing need for preservation of the Majuli River Island
define digital heritage preservation and explain how immersive technologies achieve the dual goals of safeguarding and enhancing the cultural experience of threatened heritage

L34.lecture_goal: Outline the lifecycle of building a VR experience for Majuli, from initial project concerns to technical implementation challenges.

objectives.text: identify key concerns—including cultural heritage capture, user experience, and cyber sickness—when designing the VR system for Majuli
analyze the complex tangible and intangible cultural components of Majuli and describe the multimodal data capture techniques and associated statistics used to build the heritage archive
identify the specific design, usability, and technical challenges involved in creating the immersive Majuli VR tour

L35.lecture_goal: Master the techniques for gathering and specifying requirements essential for building highly usable systems.

objectives.text: you'll be able to compare system-centered and user-centered designs, and differentiate usable end-user requirements from feasibility or design-stage considerations
you'll be able to explain the difference between functional and non-functional requirements, and describe how contextual inquiry is used to gather and justify end-user requirements for system design

L36.lecture_goal: Apply research methodologies to transform raw user observations into comprehensive, actionable usability requirements.

objectives.text: you'll be able to describe the core principles and five stages of contextual inquiry and detail the necessary planning steps for conducting it
you'll be able to identify the full lifecycle of usability research and apply the five steps of the affinity diagram method to generate initial design recommendations from raw observations
you'll be able to differentiate between the goal of identifying usability requirements and prescribing specific technical implementation details
you'll be able to apply the affinity diagram process by generating and grouping user ideas, and refine observational data to structure findings toward clear system specifications

L37.lecture_goal: Master the end-to-end process of usability requirement gathering, analysis, and specification for digital systems.

objectives.text: convert findings gathered through contextual inquiry into either design guidelines or functional requirements, and differentiate between these types
structure and document usability requirements derived from contextual inquiry findings and specify them using functional requirements within an SRS document
identify and categorize diverse user groups using field research to define the specific scope of a VR system
analyze key challenges in VR/AR development, such as cyber sickness and disorientation, and explain how requirement gathering methods address them
identify the key topics of usability requirement gathering, analysis, and specification

L38.lecture_goal: Develop the skills needed to plan, structure, and refine interfaces for effective immersive and extended reality experiences.

objectives.text: you'll be able to explain how to initiate a design process and describe interface and interaction design within the design-prototype-evaluate cycle
you'll be able to explain Shneiderman's Eight Golden Rules and apply them to designing diverse interactive and extended reality systems
you'll be able to identify the specialized types of interaction techniques crucial for designing immersive VR and MR experiences

L39.lecture_goal: understand the foundational concepts and advanced techniques used to interact with objects within immersive virtual and augmented reality systems.

objectives.text: identify and differentiate the three broad categories of immersive interaction techniques, and explain the two fundamental types of object interaction (selection and manipulation) and the factors influencing selection technique choice

you'll be able to compare and contrast various methods of selecting virtual objects, including hand tracking, go-go, prism, intent-driven techniques, pointing-based methods, and image plane and volumetric selection techniques used in VR/AR systems

identify and describe various object manipulation techniques, differentiating between direct and indirect methods, and describing advanced bimanual and hybrid techniques like Spindle, Spindle Plus Wheel, and HOMER

L40.lecture_goal: Master the principles of designing complex, navigable, and interactable immersive virtual environments.

objectives.text: analyze the components, types, and locomotion methods used for navigation in immersive experiences
compare walking-based locomotion techniques, including full gait, partial gait, and gait negation
classify and describe steering-based and selection-based and manipulation-based locomotion techniques in VR systems
define wayfinding, identify necessary knowledge for building a cognitive map, and describe techniques for providing effective wayfinding support
describe various interaction techniques for system control and summarize core concepts of immersive interaction design

L41.lecture_goal: design and critically evaluate the components and design philosophy of a cohesive, engaging virtual or augmented reality system.

objectives.text: relate foundational VR principles and design content for an immersive tour
describe and integrate technical elements to enhance visual realism and system interaction
explain how spatial orientation and navigation are managed within a virtual system
evaluate design techniques to minimize negative physical responses in immersive experiences

L42.lecture_goal: Master the essential methodologies for designing, prototyping, and iteratively evaluating interactive XR systems.

objectives.text: explain the concepts of XR system implementation and outline how the design-prototype-evaluate cycle drives the iterative stages of interactive system development
differentiate between various prototyping techniques, comparing characteristics like fidelity (low/medium/high), horizontal versus vertical approaches, and specialized methods such as Wizard of Oz

L43.lecture_goal: Master the various methodologies required to assess the usability and effectiveness of system prototypes throughout the design lifecycle.

objectives.text: compare the different types of prototypes and identify the appropriate evaluation strategies, including the process for conducting a quick usability evaluation
execute the cognitive walkthrough procedure and apply heuristic evaluation techniques to assess the usability of a prototype

L44.lecture_goal: Master the processes of deploying, optimizing, and evaluating immersive virtual reality experiences.

objectives.text: you'll be able to compare post-task and post-session user evaluation methodologies (such as ASQ and SUS) and identify specific questionnaires used to evaluate comfort and sickness in immersive XR experiences

you'll be able to compare implementation methods, technologies, and optimization strategies used to deploy VR experiences on different platforms, utilizing case studies like distinct VR tours based on 360-degree images and 3D models

L45.lecture_goal: master the principles of system evaluation by differentiating between various testing methods and understanding the full scope of conducting controlled empirical research.

objectives.text: distinguish between code testing and empirical evaluation, and recognize the limitations of quick prototype evaluations versus rigorous empirical studies

describe the stages of empirical research, differentiate between testable and non-testable research questions, explain the role of variables (independent and dependent), and outline the steps for designing an empirical study

L46.lecture_goal: Master the complete process of designing, executing, and analyzing empirical usability studies.

objectives.text: differentiate between testable and untestable research questions to guide empirical usability studies
structure an empirical evaluation by carefully selecting participants, tasks, and designing the assignment method
apply statistical significance testing to determine if experimental results are reliable or due to chance

L47.lecture_goal: Evaluate the practical application of empirical methods to assess the effectiveness and user experience of virtual reality implementations.

objectives.text: relate theoretical concepts of empirical evaluation to practical case studies and analyze methods used to measure user engagement, presence, and comfort in virtual environments
describe the complete experimental setup, including participant characteristics, technical apparatus, methods, scales, and methodological choices for implementing a controlled VR study
describe the stages of controlled experiments, explain how system implementation results demonstrate good presence, and analyze empirical data regarding user experience and cyber sickness
outline the systematic steps of empirical evaluation, from defining parameters to drawing evidence-based conclusions

L48.lecture_goal: compare and contrast traditional sequential system implementation with modern Agile development approaches.

objectives.text: you'll be able to outline the stages of the interactive system development life cycle and explain the limitations and documentation challenges associated with traditional sequential implementation
you'll be able to describe the core principles and process flow of the Agile development approach, and summarize the steps for designing and evaluating system prototypes

L49.lecture_goal: determine strategies and principles necessary for designing and optimizing effective and comfortable virtual reality experiences.

objectives.text: recall foundational concepts regarding extended reality systems, human factors, and usable system development; distinguish between optimized experience and optimized resource utilization as two perspectives of VR optimization

identify and categorize the internal and external factors that cause cyber sickness in VR experiences; understand how to minimize cyber sickness by reducing navigation duration or distance while maximizing user presence

compare user-controlled and system-controlled virtual reality tours and categorize virtual locomotion techniques; explain the benefits and limitations of system-controlled experiences to achieve presence; explain why matching the travel speed to the user's realistic walking speed is vital for enhancing presence and optimizing VR experience

L50.lecture_goal: Describe the development and validation of a realistic walking behavior model to optimize VR navigation.

objectives.text: describe the process and purpose of developing a realistic walking behavior model for system-controlled VR navigation
describe the subject's participant characteristics and the structure of the experimental setup
describe the methodology for collecting and calculating instantaneous step frequency from video recordings
compare the observed CISO movement pattern to the mathematical principles of the Fourier series to propose a model
apply a visual gain factor to synchronize virtual scene speed with perceived natural walking behavior
compare constant versus natural walking speeds to validate the effectiveness of a VR perception model
compare the effects of constant versus instantaneous walking speeds on realism and user preference in virtual reality
explain the limitations of the realistic walking speed model in addressing cyber sickness while maximizing presence

L51.lecture_goal: Design an optimized virtual reality tour path by applying graph theory and time-constrained algorithms to minimize user exposure and mitigate cybersickness.

objectives.text: you'll be able to explain how controlling exposure duration addresses cyber sickness, analyze how physical parameters like world size and travel speed influence duration, define semi-interactive tours, and compare two optimization strategies for tour duration under time constraints

you'll be able to model a virtual experience as a weighted graph, derive travel time calculations, and adapt minimum-time pathfinding algorithms (like TSP) to optimize tour duration while acknowledging real-world constraints

L52.lecture_goal: master the techniques required to formulate and optimize efficient VR paths for maximizing engagement and coverage of critical points of interest.

objectives.text: compare the objectives of path planning, contrasting minimizing travel time for all nodes versus maximizing the capture of points of interest within a defined time limit
formulate a constrained optimization problem to maximize the total importance of visited Points of Interest (POIs) within a specific time threshold
apply a multi-stage algorithm to determine the optimal VR path by incorporating both weighted importance of POIs and the impact of waiting time

L53.lecture_goal: understand the methodologies and frameworks required to design and execute optimized virtual reality experiences.

objectives.text: you'll be able to contrast the optimal path approach with the optimal path under time constraint approach for VR navigation optimization
you'll be able to design, convert, and determine optimal paths for system-controlled VR tours by modeling a physical site as a usable graph and applying solvers like TSP and VRPP
you'll be able to identify the two distinct types of optimization necessary in XR environments: psychophysiological experience optimization and resource optimization

L54.lecture_goal: understand the relationship between human visual perception, hardware architecture, and the process of rendering digital imagery in advanced graphical systems.

objectives.text: distinguish between optimizing the VR experience and minimizing the resource requirements of a VR system, and explain why specialized hardware is necessary to manage rendering and computer graphics issues in Virtual Reality
explain the fundamental difference between how human visual perception works and how computers represent data in binary

identify the major components of a graphics system, compare vector and raster scanning methods, explain the function of the frame buffer, and describe how color is perceived through RGB principles and the 3D graphics pipeline

L55.lecture_goal: analyze how complex 3D objects are represented and optimized throughout the graphics rendering pipeline.

objectives.text: explain the stage-wise process of the 3D graphics pipeline, from object representation to pixel-level description

compare the necessity of intricate object representation with the requirements for efficient rendering processes, and categorize 3D object representation techniques, including explaining the mechanism of point sample rendering

differentiate between Boundary Representation, Mesh, and Spline representations for defining virtual objects, and distinguish between general space partitioning and specialized techniques for representing complex objects
distinguish between the fixed stages and the potentially variable sequence of the 3D graphics pipeline

L56.lecture_goal: Master the core principles of 3D graphics pipelines and lighting models necessary for efficient VR resource optimization.

objectives.text: identify the critical stages of the 3D graphics pipeline and describe the modeling and lighting stages
apply geometric transformations using basic and composite matrices to accurately position objects within a scene
compare lighting and shading models, analyze how to calculate reflected light intensity using simple models, and modify these models using attenuation factors for realistic VR effects
model the color perception and intensity calculations required for single and multiple colored light sources
explain how continuous intensity values generated by a lighting model are mapped and converted to discrete color levels supported by a device

L57.lecture_goal: master the fundamental concepts and transformations within the graphics pipeline for VR resource optimization.

objectives.text: relate VR resource optimization challenges to core computer graphics concepts
explain how the 3D viewing pipeline projects a scene onto a 2D screen using various transformations
differentiate between and apply perspective and parallel projections, and describe viewport mapping
analyze the role of clipping and hidden surface removal in optimizing the graphics rendering pipeline

L58.lecture_goal: Analyze the computational and architectural trade-offs required to efficiently render complex scenes in a virtual reality environment.

objectives.text: describe the structure of the 3D graphics pipeline, including coordinate mapping, applying Bresenham's algorithm, and implementing anti-aliasing to handle computational complexity
explain how graphics libraries and APIs abstract low-level system details and describe the layered architectural components used in VR system graphics
describe the fundamental architecture of a GPU and explain how specialized hardware exploits parallelism to implement the 3D graphics pipeline for high-performance VR rendering

L59.lecture_goal: Analyze methods for optimizing VR resources to ensure effective deployment on diverse hardware platforms.

objectives.text: analyze how computer graphics pipeline knowledge informs practical decision-making in large-scale VR systems, and explain how cloud computing and optimization strategies address the computational and storage challenges of rich VR content
describe resource optimization strategies, such as compression and feature removal, to deploy VR on limited hardware

L60.lecture_goal: guide students through the initial theoretical frameworks and practical tools necessary for starting XR system development.

objectives.text: explain how to transition from theoretical XR knowledge to actual system development, and how to convert acquired concepts into practical ideas using programming environments
identify the purpose of a support platform for prioritizing immersive experiences, and describe Unity's function as a cross-platform engine and the role of Unity Hub in its management
differentiate between Virtual, Mixed, and Augmented Reality system types, compare the Scene and Game Views, and define Unity's fundamental concepts such as Assets, Scenes, GameObjects, and Prefabs

L61.lecture_goal: master the essential components and processes required to link theoretical computer graphics concepts to practical implementation within the Unity environment for XR development.

objectives.text: understand how the Unity developer environment supports the graphics pipeline and rendering process, including defining 3D objects (models, meshes, materials, textures), setting up scene elements, and utilizing native libraries such as OpenGL and Vulkan
explain how realistic movement and physical interactions are achieved by using Unity's physics components (like rigid bodies and colliders) and managing complex animation structures (using joints)
describe how to implement audio immersion and modify sound effects using Unity's specific components

L62.lecture_goal: master the fundamentals of Unity game and AR development by linking theoretical scripting concepts to practical application using C# and external SDKs.

objectives.text: understand how scripting (C#) is used to customize the behavior of game objects in the Unity environment and create and describe the core structure and execution functions of a Unity C# script
control object behavior by utilizing variables, checking values in the Inspector, managing object destruction, and distinguishing between prebuilt and user-defined functions within Unity

apply advanced scripting concepts such as prefab instantiation, conditional logic, and coroutines, and utilize coding constructs and editor features to control object behavior and deploy an immersive system
integrate specialized platform functions by understanding how to use external SDKs and setting up and configuring a marker-based Augmented Reality (AR) application within Unity
configure and deploy an augmented reality application for an Android platform, and describe the mechanics and components of a marker-based AR system using the Vuforia SDK in Unity
relate theoretical concepts to practical functionalities by utilizing development environments and importing SDKs to enhance a Unity project

L63.lecture_goal: Consolidate the course learning by summarizing its structure and defining the foundational objective of XR.

objectives.text: you'll be able to outline the overall course structure, including the key topics and scope of Modules 3 through 6
you'll be able to understand how XR serves as a base for extending knowledge in allied disciplines
